subject: business-studies
title: Taylor & McGregor Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll meet Taylor's piece-rate approach and McGregor's X vs Y views of staff.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies — Taylor's scientific management and McGregor X/Y theory applied.
final_note: You can describe Taylor's piece-rate model and contrast McGregor's Theory X with Theory Y.

concepts.def: Scientific manager — money is the main motivator
McGregor: staff are lazy and need control
McGregor: staff are willing and need empowering
Giving staff power to make decisions

walkthroughs.body_html:
Frederick Taylor thought workers were motivated mainly by money.

He pushed piece-rate pay, tight supervision and scientifically planned tasks for max output.

Theory X: staff are lazy, avoid work, need close control and threats.

Theory Y: staff enjoy work, are creative and self-motivated when trusted.

A factory paying £2 per item finished encourages speed (Taylor) — but can hurt quality.

A tech firm with flexitime + project ownership reflects Theory Y management.

mcqs.q: What is operations management concerned with?
options: Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
The design and control of the production process and business operations — converting inputs into outputs efficiently. It includes capacity, quality, supply chain, and process improvement.
Operations management is the same as general management.
